1997  ·  RECRUIT | Daniel is sixteen. His mother has found a “family | companion” programme on a message board and | printed its questionnaire for him. It asks whether he | has corrected the way he walks, talks and sits. | Anonymous boards and mailing lists were used by | conversion practices in their move online: a name for | “the problem”, and a way out of it, offered to | whoever searched. | Or press the panel to read here. | Sources | 2003  ·  AUDIT | Daniel is an adult, in the same room. The programme | now lives on his computer as software. Every morning it | asks how he is — Steady, Struggling, Grateful or Tired | — and keeps the answer. It watches who he talks to; | when a message arrives from someone outside, the | programme sees it first. Peer accountability, and | software that logged browsing and reported it to a | partner, are documented; the streak and the machine | that reads his messages are the piece's own | compression of them. Here they carry the demand to | change without anyone saying it out loud. | 2016  ·  GOVERN | Vera works from her room, correcting other women’s | writing for a platform — lesbian women, writing | about their own lives — one rule at a time: remove | anything unresolved, add the scripture. One | afternoon the group chat on her phone is about a | law: Malta has just made practices like hers an | offence, unanimously. Nobody in the room says | anything. Content rules and moderation work were | among the tools these networks used to reach | people at scale. In this room nobody is treated; the | writing is edited. | 2026  ·  RESURGE | Maya’s session is restored for her before she has touched anything. A | companion finishes her search and suggests she wants to stop. Her record | keeps her old name “for continuity of care”. Her photographs come back | improved. A headset offers an immersive session. Then a friend’s | invitation, inside that same headset, leads her somewhere the system | cannot classify — a room where being trans is fine — and the update fails. | This room is inferred. Around it, the record is not: in May 2026 the | European Commission answered more than a million people asking for a | ban on conversion practices with a non-binding recommendation, and | declined to propose a law; organised campaigns against trans people’s | care run across Europe. The room extends patterns that are already | documented — autocomplete, retained records, photo enhancement, | “support” agents — into a system that presents itself as care. What it | cannot classify is other people.
